transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Ever since I was there during that shooting, the scene keeps replaying in my head all day and I can’t shut it off. It's like a loop that just won't stop, and I'm really struggling to get through my days.
Can you tell me more about what happens when these memories replay in your head, do you feel like you're reliving the shooting all over again?

Yes, it’s like a loop that starts up out of nowhere, even when I'm making a delivery or just sitting in church. I suddenly see those people running past my van and hear the gunshots, and I just freeze up and can't focus on anything else until it slowly fades. It really does feel like I'm right back in that moment.
When these memories replay and you feel like you're reliving the shooting, do you feel disconnected from your body or like you're observing yourself from outside?
No, I don't feel disconnected from my body or like I'm watching myself from the outside. It actually feels incredibly real and internal, like I'm trapped right inside my own head when it happens.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of the shooting, or are there things you used to enjoy that you've stopped doing since it happened?

Yes, absolutely. I’ve been avoiding my delivery routes on the Westside, and I won't pull into apartment complexes or crowded gas stations anymore. I also stopped going to my basketball league and choir practice, and I completely shut down if my mom or coworkers try to ask me about that night because my chest just tightens up.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats, even when you're in safe environments, like always checking for exits or watching for suspicious people?

I definitely feel constantly on edge and tense all the time, like my body is always waiting for something bad to happen. But I haven't really noticed myself doing specific things like checking for exits or actively scanning the area for suspicious people.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'on edge' and 'tense all the time', is it more of a physical feeling, an emotional state, or a combination of both?

It’s definitely a combination of both. Physically, my whole body flinches and my heart pounds at any sudden noise like a car backfiring, and I keep jerking awake in bed at night. Emotionally, I'm so wound up that the smallest things make me snap and raise my voice at people.
Have you experienced any difficulty falling or staying asleep, or have you been having nightmares related to the shooting?

Yes, my sleep has been terrible all week. I lie in bed exhausted, but as soon as I close my eyes, I feel like I'm back in that parking lot and I toss and turn for hours. When I finally do doze off, I jerk awake at every little noise outside, terrified that someone is about to start shooting again.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened during the shooting, or do you blame yourself for anything related to that event?

No, I don't feel responsible or guilty for the shooting itself, since I was just there delivering packages. I only feel guilty about how I've been snapping at my family and my boss lately. I know they're just trying to help, and I feel really bad about taking my stress out on them.

You mentioned feeling on edge and tense, but not specifically checking for exits or scanning for suspicious people. Have you noticed any other behaviors or thoughts that could be considered as always being 'on guard', such as an exaggerated startle response to sudden noises or an inability to relax in quiet environments?

Yes, I definitely experience that. Ever since the shooting, I jump out of my skin at any sudden sound—like a car backfiring or someone dropping something loud in the warehouse. My whole body flinches, my heart starts pounding like crazy, and it takes me a really long time to calm down even after I realize there's no danger.
Have you noticed any difficulties with concentration or memory since the shooting, such as trouble focusing at work or forgetting things that you normally would remember?

Yes, I'm struggling with both. I have blank spaces in my memory from that night, like I can't remember how many shots were fired or where the shooter was. On top of that, when the memories start replaying, I just freeze up and can't focus on my work or think about anything else.

You mentioned earlier that during these memory replays, you don't feel disconnected from your body, but can you tell me if there are any moments where you feel like you're in a daze or spaced out, separate from what's happening around you?
No, I wouldn't say I feel like I'm in a daze or separated from my surroundings. It's more that I just feel completely frozen and locked into the memory itself when it happens.
Can you estimate how long these intrusive memories and associated symptoms have been affecting you since the shooting occurred?
All of these symptoms started in the days right after the shooting in the apartment parking lot. It has been going on for about a week now.
You mentioned that these symptoms have been affecting you for about a week now, do you think they've been getting worse, staying the same, or possibly improving at all over this past week?

They’ve been intense and constant ever since it happened, and it feels like things are getting harder to manage because the consequences are piling up. I’m constantly exhausted and on edge without any relief, my boss is warning me that my job is on the line, and I keep snapping at my family. It definitely feels like it's getting worse to deal with because of all that pressure.

You mentioned that your symptoms have been constant and intense since the shooting, but can you tell me if there have been any days or moments within the past week where your symptoms seemed to lessen or where you felt slightly better, even if it was brief?

No, I haven't really had any moments of relief or felt any better, not even for a little bit. I feel completely on edge all the time, and the shooting is constantly replaying in my head throughout the day. It honestly feels like there is absolutely no break from it.

You mentioned the symptoms have been constant for about a week, can you confirm if you've experienced any symptom-free moments or periods where the intrusive memories and associated distress significantly decreased, even if briefly, since the shooting occurred?

No, I can confirm that I haven't had any symptom-free moments at all. The scene keeps replaying in my head in a loop throughout the day, and even when a flashback slowly fades, I'm still constantly on edge and jumpy. The distress never truly goes away, so there is just no break.

You've mentioned that your symptoms started right after the shooting and have been constant for about a week, but can you clarify if you've had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt like you were back to your normal self or where the symptoms significantly decreased since the incident?

No, I haven't felt like my normal self for even a second since that night. I'm constantly exhausted and on edge, and the loop of the shooting in my head hasn't let up at all. It has just been one continuous, draining week without any breaks.
You've had these symptoms for about a week now, but can you tell me if you're concerned that these symptoms might last longer than a month, or do you think they will resolve on their own soon?

Since it's only been about a week since the shooting, I honestly don't know how long this will last or if it will resolve on its own. I'm just really worried because of how much it's already affecting my job and my life, and I desperately hope it stops soon.
Do you think your symptoms will persist beyond a month or do you expect them to resolve sooner?
I'm really not sure, and I haven't thought much about how long it will last. It's only been a week since the shooting, and right now I just desperately want it to stop.
Do you think your symptoms will likely continue beyond a month from now, or do you expect they might improve before then?

I really hope they improve soon because of how much they are disrupting my life and putting my job at risk. But honestly, I'm not sure if they will actually go away on their own since everything feels so intense right now. I just can't see past how bad things are today.
Do you think it's possible that your symptoms could continue for more than a month, or do you believe they will start to improve before that?

Since it’s only been about a week since the shooting, I honestly don't know if this will last more than a month or if it will start to get better. But because everything is so intense and constant right now, I am deeply worried that these symptoms might continue for a very long time.
Do you think it's possible that your symptoms could continue for more than a month, or do you believe they will start to improve before that?
I'm really not sure and I haven't thought about how long this will last. I just desperately hope it stops soon because it's already affecting my job and my daily life so much.
Do you think your symptoms will likely last more than a month from now, or do you expect they might improve before then?

To be honest, it’s only been about a week since the shooting, so I really don’t know if this is going to last longer than a month. I desperately hope it gets better soon, but right now everything feels so intense and constant that I just don't know if it will go away on its own.
Are you concerned that these symptoms will continue to affect you for more than a month, or do you think they might start to improve before that?
I'm really not sure what to expect since it has only been about a week. I just desperately hope they will go away soon because of how much they are already affecting my life and my job.
Do you think your symptoms will likely continue beyond a month from the shooting, or do you expect they might improve before then, considering how intense they have been for the past week?

Since it’s only been about a week since the shooting, I really don't know if this will last beyond a month. Because everything is so intense and overwhelming right now, it honestly feels like it might never go away, and I'm just desperate for some relief.

Considering your symptoms have been constant for about a week, do you think they will start to decrease in intensity or frequency within the next few weeks, or do you expect them to remain as intense as they are now?
I'm really not sure if they will start to decrease or stay this intense. Right now, everything feels completely overwhelming and I just can't see how or when it's going to get any better.
Do you think your symptoms are likely to improve on their own within the next few weeks, or are you concerned that they may persist or even worsen over time?

I honestly don't know if they will get better on their own or not. Right now, it just feels like this nightmare is never going to stop, and I'm really worried about what's going to happen to my life if it doesn't.
Are you concerned that if these symptoms do last more than a month, it could significantly impact your ability to function in daily life and at work?

I am extremely concerned because it is already severely impacting my life after just one week—my boss warned me my job is on the line because I've been calling in sick and dodging routes, and I've already had to stop going to choir and basketball. If this goes on for a month, I am absolutely terrified that I will lose my job completely and just fall apart.

Given that your symptoms have been constant for about a week, do you think they will start to decrease in intensity or frequency within the next few weeks, or do you expect them to remain as intense as they are now?

I really don't know what to expect and can't say if they'll start to get better or stay this intense. I'm just hoping they will improve soon because the way I feel right now is completely overwhelming.
Do you think that if your symptoms were to continue beyond a month, you would be able to cope with them on your own, or would you need professional help to manage them?

I definitely feel like I would need professional help to manage this. It's only been about a week and my life is already falling apart—my job is on the line and I've had to stop doing things I love like choir and basketball. I can't imagine trying to cope with this on my own for a whole month, which is why I accepted the referral to this clinic in the first place.

Considering your symptoms have been constant for about a week, and you're unsure if they will improve, do you think seeking professional help now could make a difference in how long these symptoms last or their impact on your life?

Yes, I really hope so because I'm desperate for things to change before I lose everything. My job is on the line and I've already had to skip choir and basketball, so I accepted the referral from my church's outreach program in the hopes that a professional can help me get back to normal and stop feeling so on edge.
